revealWordProblem.title: Apply: The Pizza Fundraiser
revealWordProblem.text: The 6th-grade class is buying pizza for a fundraiser. Pizza Palace sells 3 pizzas for $27.00, and Pizza Town sells 5 pizzas for $42.50. The class needs 15 pizzas. Find each pizzeria's unit rate (price per pizza), decide which one is the better buy, and figure out how much 15 pizzas will cost there. Show your work.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Pizza Palace: $27.00 ÷ 3 = $9.00 per pizza. Pizza Town: $42.50 ÷ 5 = $8.50 per pizza. Since $8.50 is the lower unit rate, the class should order from Pizza Town. 15 pizzas × $8.50 = $127.50.

questions.stem: Which is the better buy: 6 bouncy balls for $4.50 or 10 bouncy balls for $8.00?
choices: They cost the same per ball
choiceFeedback: Find the price per ball for each: divide cost by quantity.
Compare the unit prices.
Make sure you're dividing cost by quantity for each option.
hints: You can't compare $4.50 and $8.00 straight across — the packs hold different numbers of balls.
Find each pack's price for ONE ball (cost ÷ number of balls), then compare the two unit prices.
Start with the first deal: $4.50 ÷ 6. Then compute $8.00 ÷ 10 and see which per-ball price is lower.
questions.stemEs: ¿Cuál es la mejor compra: 6 pelotas saltarinas por $4.50 o 10 pelotas saltarinas por $8.00?
questions.explanationEs: $4.50 ÷ 6 = $0.75 cada una. $8.00 ÷ 10 = $0.80 cada una. $0.75 < $0.80, así que 6 por $4.50 es la mejor compra.
hintsEs: No puedes comparar $4.50 y $8.00 directamente: los paquetes traen cantidades distintas de pelotas.
Halla el precio de UNA pelota en cada paquete (costo ÷ número de pelotas) y luego compara los dos precios unitarios.
Empieza con la primera oferta: $4.50 ÷ 6. Luego calcula $8.00 ÷ 10 y ve qué precio por pelota es menor.

questions.stem: A faucet drips 15 ounces of water in 5 minutes. What is the unit rate?
choiceFeedback: Divide: 15 ounces ÷ 5 minutes.
Find the rate per minute.
You divided the minutes by the ounces. For ounces per minute, ounces go first.
hints: The unit rate here is ounces per ONE minute — 15 ounces spread across 5 minutes.
Divide the ounces by the minutes so the time becomes 1 minute.
Set up 15 ÷ 5 ounces per minute.
questions.stemEs: Una llave gotea 15 onzas de agua en 5 minutos. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad?
hintsEs: La tasa unitaria aquí son onzas por UN minuto: 15 onzas repartidas en 5 minutos.
Divide las onzas entre los minutos para que el tiempo se vuelva 1 minuto.
Plantea 15 ÷ 5 onzas por minuto.

questions.stem: A printer prints 42 pages in 6 minutes. How many pages does it print in 15 minutes at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Unit rate: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 pages per minute. In 15 minutes: 7 × 15 = 105 pages.
choiceFeedback: Divide: 42 pages ÷ 6 minutes.
Find the rate per minute.
Not quite. Unit rate: 42 ÷ 6 = ___ pages per minute.
hints: This takes two steps: first find pages per ONE minute, then scale up to 15 minutes.
Divide to get the unit rate, then multiply that rate by the new time.
Step 1: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 pages each minute. Step 2: multiply that rate by 15 minutes.
questions.stemEs: Una impresora imprime 42 páginas en 6 minutos. ¿Cuántas páginas imprime en 15 minutos al mismo ritmo?
questions.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 páginas por minuto. En 15 minutos: 7 × 15 = 105 páginas.
hintsEs: Esto toma dos pasos: halla primero las páginas por UN minuto y luego amplía a 15 minutos.
Divide para obtener la tasa unitaria, luego multiplica esa tasa por el tiempo nuevo.
Paso 1: 42 ÷ 6 = 7 páginas por minuto. Paso 2: multiplica esa tasa por 15 minutos.

reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake in Solve Problems with Unit Rates is comparing the total prices instead of the cost per item — the deal with the smaller total can still cost more per unit. Always reduce each option to its unit rate before you decide, then pick the lower one.

level1.explanation: Store A: $8 ÷ 5 = $1.60. Store B: $5.25 ÷ 3 = $1.75. $1.60 < $1.75, so Store A is cheaper per notebook.
choiceFeedback: Find the price per notebook for each store.
Compare the unit prices.
Which store has the lower price per notebook?
hints: Each store sells a different number of notebooks, so compare the price of ONE notebook at each store.
Divide cost by quantity for each store, then pick the smaller per-notebook price.
Store A: $8 ÷ 5 notebooks. Then compute Store B: $5.25 ÷ 3, and compare the two prices.
level1.stemEs: La tienda A vende 5 cuadernos por $8. La tienda B vende 3 cuadernos por $5.25. ¿Cuál tiene el precio más bajo por cuaderno?

There are 12 inches in every foot.

hints: The key fact: 1 foot = 12 inches. You have 7 feet and want inches.
Going from a BIGGER unit (feet) to a SMALLER unit (inches) means you multiply.

level1.stem: (Lesson 3.10) How many feet are in 3 yards?
choiceFeedback: Multiply 3 by 3 (feet per yard).
There are 3 feet in every yard.
Not quite. 1 yard = ___ feet.
hints: The key fact: 1 yard = 3 feet. You have 3 yards and want feet.
Big unit (yards) to small unit (feet) means multiply by the conversion factor 3.

De unidad grande (yardas) a unidad pequeña (pies) significa multiplicar por el factor de conversión 3.
Plantea 3 × 3: tres yardas, cada una de 3 pies.

choiceFeedback: Multiply 150 by 0.20, or divide by 5.
Not quite. Multiply: 0.20 × 150 = ___.
Try converting 20% to a decimal or fraction first.
hints: '20% of 150' means you want a PART of 150 — the answer should be smaller than 150.
Convert the percent to a decimal, then multiply: Part = Percent × Base.
Write 20% as 0.20, then set up 0.20 × 150. (Shortcut: 10% of 150 is 15 — double it.)
hintsEs: '20% de 150' significa que quieres una PARTE de 150: la respuesta debe ser menor que 150.
Convierte el porcentaje en decimal y luego multiplica: Parte = Porcentaje × Base.
Escribe 20% como 0.20 y plantea 0.20 × 150. (Atajo: 10% de 150 es 15; duplícalo.)

choiceFeedback: 50% is half — divide 84 by 2.

Not quite. Multiply: 0.50 × 84 = ___.

Finding 50% of a number is the same as dividing that number by 2.

hintsEs: 50% es un porcentaje amigable: significa exactamente la mitad del número.
Hallar el 50% de un número es lo mismo que dividir ese número entre 2.
Plantea 84 ÷ 2, o compruébalo con la fórmula: 0.50 × 84.

level2.stem: A machine dispenses 24 tokens in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many tokens does it dispense in 10 minutes?
level2.explanation: Unit rate: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens per minute. In 10 minutes: 8 × 10 = 80 tokens.
choiceFeedback: First find tokens per minute: 24 ÷ 3. Then multiply by 12 minutes.
Find the unit rate, then use it to find the answer for 12 minutes.
You need to find how many tokens per minute first.
hints: Two steps: find tokens per ONE minute first, then stretch that rate to 10 minutes.
Divide tokens by minutes for the unit rate, then multiply the rate by the new time.
Step 1: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 tokens each minute. Step 2: multiply that rate by 10 minutes.
level2.stemEs: Una máquina despacha 24 fichas en 3 minutos. A ese ritmo, ¿cuántas fichas despacha en 10 minutos?
level2.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 fichas por minuto. En 10 minutos: 8 × 10 = 80 fichas.
hintsEs: Dos pasos: halla primero las fichas por UN minuto y luego extiende esa tasa a 10 minutos.
Divide las fichas entre los minutos para la tasa unitaria, luego multiplica la tasa por el tiempo nuevo.
Paso 1: 24 ÷ 3 = 8 fichas por minuto. Paso 2: multiplica esa tasa por 10 minutos.

level2.stem: A factory produces 360 widgets in 8 hours. At the same rate, how many widgets are produced in a 12-hour shift?
level2.explanation: Unit rate: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets per hour. In 12 hours: 45 × 12 = 540 widgets.
choiceFeedback: First find widgets per hour: 360 ÷ 8. Then multiply by 20 hours.
Find the unit rate, then use it to find the answer for 20 hours.
Start by finding how many widgets per hour.
hints: Two steps: find widgets per ONE hour first, then scale up to the 12-hour shift.
Divide widgets by hours for the unit rate, then multiply that rate by 12.
Step 1: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 widgets each hour. Step 2: multiply that rate by 12 hours.
level2.stemEs: Una fábrica produce 360 piezas en 8 horas. Al mismo ritmo, ¿cuántas piezas se producen en un turno de 12 horas?
level2.explanationEs: Tasa por unidad: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 piezas por hora. En 12 horas: 45 × 12 = 540 piezas.
hintsEs: Dos pasos: halla primero los artículos por UNA hora y luego escálalo al turno de 12 horas.
Divide los artículos entre las horas para la tasa unitaria y luego multiplica esa tasa por 12.
Paso 1: 360 ÷ 8 = 45 artículos por hora. Paso 2: multiplica esa tasa por 12 horas.

level2.stem: The snack bar compares two popcorn deals: 12 oz for $3.00 or 20 oz for $4.00. Which is the better buy?
choices: They cost the same per ounce
choiceFeedback: Find price per ounce for each.
Compare unit rates.
You have everything you need — each deal gives a total price and a total number of ounces, and that is enough to find a price per ounce.
level2.stemEs: El puesto de bocadillos compara dos ofertas de palomitas: 12 oz por $3.00 o 20 oz por $4.00. ¿Cuál es la mejor compra?
level2.explanationEs: 12 oz: $3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 por oz. 20 oz: $4.00 ÷ 20 = $0.20 por oz. $0.20 < $0.25, así que 20 oz por $4.00 es la mejor compra.
hints: Different package sizes can only be compared once both are priced per ounce.
Divide each deal's price by its number of ounces to get a cost per ounce.
Start with the 12-ounce deal: $3.00 ÷ 12. Then do the same for the 20-ounce deal and compare the two.
hintsEs: Los envases de distinto tamaño solo se pueden comparar cuando ambos tienen precio por onza.
Divide el precio de cada oferta entre su número de onzas para obtener el costo por onza.
Empieza con la oferta de 12 onzas: $3.00 ÷ 12. Luego haz lo mismo con la de 20 onzas y compara.

level2.stem: The delivery van brings arcade supplies 150 miles in 3 hours. What is the unit rate in miles per hour?
choiceFeedback: Divide 150 by 3.
Unit rate is miles per hour.

level2.stemEs: La camioneta de reparto lleva suministros para el salón de juegos 150 millas en 3 horas. ¿Cuál es la tasa por unidad en millas por hora?
hints: 'Miles per hour' tells you the distance covered in exactly 1 hour.
Divide the distance by the time: miles ÷ hours.
Set up 150 ÷ 3 and carry out that division.
hintsEs: 'Millas por hora' indica la distancia recorrida en exactamente 1 hora.
Divide la distancia entre el tiempo: millas ÷ horas.
Plantea 150 ÷ 3 y realiza esa división.

level2.stem: The ticket counter sells redemption tickets two ways: 8 tickets for $2.00 or 15 tickets for $3.00. Which costs less per ticket?
choices: They cost the same per ticket
choiceFeedback: Find price per ticket for each.
Compare unit rates.
You can determine it — each deal gives a total cost and a total number of tickets, so divide cost by count to get a price per ticket for each.
level2.stemEs: El mostrador de boletos vende boletos de premio de dos maneras: 8 boletos por $2.00 o 15 boletos por $3.00. ¿Cuál cuesta menos por boleto?
level2.explanationEs: 8 por $2.00: $2.00 ÷ 8 = $0.25 cada uno. 15 por $3.00: $3.00 ÷ 15 = $0.20 cada uno. $0.20 < $0.25, así que 15 por $3.00 es más barato por boleto.
hints: The cheaper deal is the one with the lower price for a single ticket.
Divide each deal's total cost by its number of tickets.
Begin with 8 tickets for $2.00: $2.00 ÷ 8. Then do the same for the other deal and compare.
hintsEs: La oferta más barata es la que tiene el precio más bajo por un solo boleto.
Divide el costo total de cada oferta entre su número de boletos.
Empieza con 8 boletos por $2.00: $2.00 ÷ 8. Luego haz lo mismo con la otra oferta y compara.

choiceFeedback: That adds the 8 notebooks to the $20. Find the price of ONE notebook first: 20 divided by 8.
That adds $1 for each of the 6 extra notebooks. Each notebook costs $2.50, so 6 more cost $15.
That doubles the $20, which would buy 16 notebooks. Multiply the unit price by 14.

level3.prompt: Two arcade supply companies offer token deals. Company X: 300 tokens for $36. Company Y: 500 tokens for $55. The arcade needs 1,000 tokens. Find the unit rate for each company, determine which is cheaper per token, and calculate the total cost of buying 1,000 tokens from the better deal.
level3.sentenceFrame: Company X charges $___ per token and Company Y charges $___ per token. The better deal is Company ___ because ___. Buying 1,000 tokens would cost $___.
level3.hint: Find the unit rate (tokens per dollar) for each company by dividing the tokens by the cost.
hints: Three jobs here: find each company's cost per token, pick the cheaper one, then price out 1,000 tokens.
Cost per token = dollars ÷ tokens for each company. Then multiply the cheaper rate by 1,000.
Company X: $36 ÷ 300 tokens = $0.12 per token. Now compute $55 ÷ 500 for Company Y and compare before scaling to 1,000.
level3.explanation: Company X charges $36 ÷ 300 = $0.12 per token and Company Y charges $55 ÷ 500 = $0.11 per token, so Y is cheaper for each token even though its package costs more. At $0.11 per token, 1,000 tokens cost 1,000 × $0.11 = $110.
level3.explanationEs: La Compañía X cobra $36 ÷ 300 = $0.12 por ficha y la Compañía Y cobra $55 ÷ 500 = $0.11 por ficha, así que Y es más barata por cada ficha aunque su paquete cueste más. A $0.11 por ficha, 1,000 fichas cuestan 1,000 × $0.11 = $110.
level3.promptEs: Dos compañías de suministros para arcades ofrecen paquetes de fichas. Compañía X: 300 fichas por $36. Compañía Y: 500 fichas por $55. El arcade necesita 1,000 fichas. Encuentra la tasa unitaria de cada compañía, determina cuál es más barata por ficha y calcula el costo total de comprar 1,000 fichas en la mejor oferta.
hintsEs: Aquí hay tres tareas: hallar el costo por ficha de cada compañía, elegir la más barata y calcular el precio de 1,000 fichas.
Costo por ficha = dólares ÷ fichas en cada compañía. Luego multiplica la tasa más barata por 1,000.
Compañía X: $36 ÷ 300 fichas = $0.12 por ficha. Ahora calcula $55 ÷ 500 para la Compañía Y y compara antes de escalar a 1,000.
